unreadable_visuals: No pages were fully unreadable in the text layer during automated extraction. Some charts/tables are summarized from captions and visual inspection anchors rather than exhaustive manual redrawing.
The eBook front matter states that some third-party content may be suppressed because of electronic rights restrictions.
limitations: The figure and table counts are text-label occurrence counts from the extracted PDF text layer, not a manually deduplicated visual census.
Important graphs were curated into the graph registry for reasoning use; not every decorative or repeated graph is independently modeled.
End-of-chapter questions and applications are inventoried and used as signals for application areas but are not reproduced verbatim.
Current-data examples from the 2021 edition are not silently modernized; they are flagged where current verification is required.
Personal-finance, business, creative, and music recommendations are operational extensions designed for the user's reasoning library, not Mankiw-authored advice.

core_economic_principles.definition: Limited resources require choices among competing ends.
core_economic_principles.problem_addressed: allocation under limited time, money, labor, attention, and productive capacity
economic_mechanism: scarce resources and incentives shape choices
prices, costs, and benefits channel behavior
assumptions: resources are limited
wants exceed what can be produced
implications: choice is unavoidable
every plan consumes constrained resources
do_not_use_when: when there is no meaningful constraint
common_misinterpretations: Ignoring the ceteris paribus condition or the relevant margin.

core_economic_principles.definition: Getting more of one valued objective often requires giving up another.
core_economic_principles.problem_addressed: conflicts among goals such as efficiency and equity, leisure and income, consumption and saving
economic_mechanism: scarce resources and incentives shape choices
prices, costs, and benefits channel behavior
assumptions: choices have incompatible uses
implications: name the sacrificed objective before choosing
do_not_use_when: when a dominated option is strictly better on all dimensions
common_misinterpretations: Ignoring the ceteris paribus condition or the relevant margin.

core_economic_principles.definition: The cost of an option is the value of the best alternative sacrificed to obtain it.
core_economic_principles.problem_addressed: hidden cost of time, capital, attention, and foregone alternatives
economic_mechanism: scarce resources and incentives shape choices
prices, costs, and benefits channel behavior
assumptions: alternatives are feasible
decision maker values forgone uses
implications: cash price can understate true cost
time cost matters
do_not_use_when: when alternatives are not actually available
common_misinterpretations: Ignoring the ceteris paribus condition or the relevant margin.

core_economic_principles.definition: Incremental choices should compare incremental benefit with incremental cost.
core_economic_principles.problem_addressed: deciding whether to do a little more or less of an activity
economic_mechanism: scarce resources and incentives shape choices
prices, costs, and benefits channel behavior
assumptions: decision is divisible or adjustable
past costs are not changed by the choice
implications: continue only while marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost
do_not_use_when: all-or-nothing irreversible choices without separable margins
common_misinterpretations: Ignoring the ceteris paribus condition or the relevant margin.

core_economic_principles.definition: People respond to changes in benefits and costs.
core_economic_principles.problem_addressed: predicting behavior after prices, rules, rewards, or penalties change
economic_mechanism: scarce resources and incentives shape choices
prices, costs, and benefits channel behavior
assumptions: agents notice and respond to relevant tradeoffs
implications: policy and management systems can create unintended behavior
do_not_use_when: where behavior is dominated by constraint, habit, law, or severe uncertainty
common_misinterpretations: Ignoring the ceteris paribus condition or the relevant margin.

core_economic_principles.definition: Voluntary exchange can make parties better off by allowing specialization and access to goods/services at lower opportunity cost.
core_economic_principles.problem_addressed: creating value through exchange rather than self-sufficiency
economic_mechanism: scarce resources and incentives shape choices
prices, costs, and benefits channel behavior
assumptions: exchange is voluntary
property rights and terms are reasonably clear
implications: not every party must produce everything it consumes
do_not_use_when: when coercion, fraud, or external harms dominate
common_misinterpretations: Ignoring the ceteris paribus condition or the relevant margin.

core_economic_principles.definition: Prices and decentralized exchange often coordinate many individual decisions.
core_economic_principles.problem_addressed: allocating resources without central direction
economic_mechanism: scarce resources and incentives shape choices

cross_domain_connections.connection: Incentives and revealed behavior help test what people actually respond to.
cross_domain_connections.complementary_use: Use experiments and reframing to identify the active incentive, then use economics to analyze tradeoffs.
cross_domain_connections.tension_or_difference: Freakonomics-style stories can overfit anecdotes; economics requires assumptions and evidence.
cross_domain_connections.misuse_warning: Do not imply Mankiw endorses Think Like a Freak; this is a user-library bridge.

cross_domain_connections.connection: Risk, diversification, optionality, and ruin avoidance complement expected-value finance.
cross_domain_connections.complementary_use: Use Mankiw for present value/risk basics; use Black Swan lens for tail-risk and fragility checks.
cross_domain_connections.tension_or_difference: Textbook finance may emphasize ordinary risk more than extreme-tail epistemic uncertainty.
cross_domain_connections.misuse_warning: Do not treat diversification as protection against all ruin risk.

cross_domain_connections.connection: Customer value, segmentation, positioning, and pricing connect to demand elasticity and willingness to pay.
cross_domain_connections.complementary_use: Use economics for price response and surplus; use Kotler for market segmentation and value proposition design.
cross_domain_connections.tension_or_difference: Marketing frameworks may emphasize perception and brand where simple demand curves abstract from psychology.
cross_domain_connections.misuse_warning: Do not assume every price increase has the same elasticity across segments.

cross_domain_connections.connection: Audience behavior and release allocation can be treated as demand-testing under uncertainty.
cross_domain_connections.complementary_use: Use small experiments to measure revealed demand before scaling spend.
cross_domain_connections.tension_or_difference: Artistic goals and fan trust may matter beyond short-run conversion.
cross_domain_connections.misuse_warning: Do not buy vanity metrics or treat impressions as consumer surplus.

cross_domain_connections.connection: Scarcity, opportunity cost, and liquidity explain reserves, debt minimization, and cash-flow buffers.
cross_domain_connections.complementary_use: Use textbook logic to structure tradeoffs; apply user constraints for stability-first choices.
cross_domain_connections.tension_or_difference: Mankiw does not prescribe the user's debt-minimization philosophy.
cross_domain_connections.misuse_warning: Keep personal philosophy in operational-extension layer only.

cross_domain_connections.connection: Scorecards and accountability systems create incentives and can produce unintended behavior.
cross_domain_connections.complementary_use: Use economics to audit metrics, bottlenecks, and compensation effects.
cross_domain_connections.tension_or_difference: EOS execution tools are managerial frameworks, not textbook economic models.
cross_domain_connections.misuse_warning: Do not confuse metric improvement with real surplus or quality improvement.

cross_domain_connections.complementary_use: Use opportunity cost and transaction cost checks before adding capital or labor.
cross_domain_connections.tension_or_difference: Operational constraints can dominate textbook trade gains.
cross_domain_connections.misuse_warning: Check quality, coordination, and strategic control.

cross_domain_connections.connection: Asymmetric information affects recruiting, screening, probation, and incentives.
cross_domain_connections.complementary_use: Use signals, work samples, and staged commitments to reduce selection risk.
cross_domain_connections.tension_or_difference: A signal can be costly without being productive.
